sections.h2: Ways to sell a Federal Way house
sections.html:
Federal Way owners generally pick from an agent listing, a sale they run on their own, or a direct purchase by a buyer with no mortgage. Condition, move-out date and the size of your loan should steer the choice.

  • Agent listing: you prep the house, open it for showings and negotiate whatever the buyer's inspection turns up. It reaches the most buyers and asks the most patience.
  • Selling it yourself: pricing, marketing and paperwork are yours, including the seller disclosure statement Washington requires for improved residential property unless the buyer waives it or the transfer is exempt.
  • Direct cash purchase: no lender stands between you and closing, so loan approval cannot sink the sale. Put the written offer beside your net after loan payoff, taxes and any repairs you would otherwise fund.

sections.h2: Federal Way housing at a glance
sections.html:
The city sits in the southwest corner of King County, about 25 miles south of Seattle, and has 99,729 residents. That is 1.3 percent under the 2020 count, so growth has stalled. About 45 percent of occupied homes are rented, and the median value of an owner-occupied home is $552,800. Use that figure only as a citywide reference for your own price research.

Parks and water give some neighborhoods their pull. Steel Lake Park sits on South 312th Street, Lake Killarney is nearby, and Dash Point State Park is the only developed waterfront park inside the city. West Hylebos Wetlands Park holds a cabin built in 1883, the oldest known building in Federal Way.

A few eastern areas, including Star Lake, Camelot, Lakeland and Jovita, were named potential annexation areas. Check that your parcel is inside city limits before you contact the Permit Center. For parcel numbers, use the city's maps or the King County Parcel Viewer, or ask the Permit Center.

The seller owes it. RCW 82.45.080 places Washington's real estate excise tax on the seller, and it is due to the county treasurer on the sale date, whether or not the deed is recorded that day. A deeded Federal Way sale is reported to King County.

The state share rises in steps. At the thresholds now posted by the Department of Revenue, the first $525,000 of the price is taxed at 1.1 percent, the next slice up to $1,525,000 at 1.28 percent, the next up to $3,025,000 at 2.75 percent, and anything above that at 3 percent. Sales beginning January 1, 2027 use new cut points of $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000. A local rate is added, so your escrow officer should supply the figure for your parcel.

Pay within one month of the sale or penalty and interest begin, and unpaid tax can become a lien on the property. Ask that the excise tax show up as its own line on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: Do I need a permit or approval before selling a Federal Way house?
sections.html:
The City of Federal Way Permit Center handles building, electrical, mechanical, plumbing, demolition and fire prevention permits, along with land use and sign permits. Ask there about repairs you plan to finish before a sale, or about work a previous owner may have done without a permit.

  • Phone and email: 253-835-2607 or permitcenter@federalwaywa.gov.
  • Hours: 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday. The center is closed to the public on Wednesdays and on city holidays, including the day after Thanksgiving.
  • Applications: anything needing review goes in electronically once you request a Document Upload Link, which can take a few days. Residential electrical, mechanical and plumbing permits can be applied for online through My Building Permit.

The city will not unexpectedly demand payment by wire transfer over email. If a message claiming to be from the city asks for money, call the Permit Center before you send anything.

sections.h2: Property taxes on a Federal Way house
sections.html:
First-half taxes are due by April 30 and second-half taxes by October 31. RCW 84.56.020 makes the county treasurer the collector, so Federal Way owners pay through King County. Ask the county for the current statement on your parcel before you list, because a title company will find any open balance anyway.

When the sale closes partway through a billing period, escrow splits the bill between you and the buyer. Make sure your last payment has posted so the split starts from an accurate number.

Interstate 5 serves the city at the 348th Street, 320th Street and 272nd Street exits, and State Route 99, the Pacific Highway, runs through it. The Federal Way Transit Center on 23rd Avenue South is served by King County Metro, Pierce Transit and Sound Transit Express, and the Link light rail extension to Federal Way Downtown station opened in December 2025. Average travel time to work is 32.1 minutes, so freeway and station access is a real selling point.

Federal Way Public Schools runs the district. When you describe the house, name the nearest park, the nearest I-5 exit and the walk or drive to the station.

sections.h2: What to check before you accept an offer
sections.html:
• Get the offer in writing, with the price, the closing date and who pays each closing cost.
  • Request a payoff statement from your lender so you know the exact balance.
  • Ask the buyer for proof of funds, and whether the offer depends on repairs or an inspection.
  • Estimate your excise tax with the rates above and ask escrow for the local rate.
  • Find out whether the buyer expects the house to be emptied, and by what date.
  • Compare the net figure from each route, not the headline price alone.

RCW 64.06.020 requires the seller of improved residential property to deliver a completed disclosure statement within five business days after a written contract is accepted, unless the buyer waives it or the transfer is exempt. The buyer then has three business days after delivery to rescind.

Answer from what you actually know about the roof, plumbing, sewer and any past repairs. Having your permit history, loan payoff and tax statement in one folder before you list makes the form quicker and the buyer's questions easier to answer. A cash buyer will still ask about the same items, though usually without an appraisal or loan underwriter reviewing the answers.

faqs.q: Who pays the real estate excise tax on a house sale in Federal Way?
faqs.a: The seller. RCW 82.45.080 makes the tax the seller's obligation, and if the seller does not pay, the buyer becomes responsible. Unpaid tax can create a lien on the property.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due on a Federal Way house?
faqs.a: April 30 for the first half and October 31 for the second. Federal Way owners pay through King County, so ask the county for the current statement on your parcel.

faqs.q: Which county is Federal Way in?
faqs.a: King County. The city lies in the southwest corner of the county, about 25 miles south of Seattle, so deeds, excise tax affidavits and property tax bills for a Federal Way home go through King County offices.

faqs.q: How do I find my parcel number in Federal Way?
faqs.a: Use the city's maps or the King County Parcel Viewer, or contact the Permit Center at 253-835-2607 or permitcenter@federalwaywa.gov. You will need the number for permit questions and title work.

faqs.q: Do I have to give a buyer a seller disclosure statement?
faqs.a: Usually yes. The completed statement is due within five business days after a written contract is accepted, unless the buyer waives it or the transfer is exempt. The buyer has three business days after delivery to rescind.
